entities.summary: The Conventicle Act was a Swedish law, in effect between 21 January 1726 and 26 October 1858 in Sweden and until 1 July 1870 in Finland. The act outlawed all conventicles, or religious meetings of any kind, outside of the Lutheran Church of Sweden, with the exception of family prayer or worship. The purpose was to prevent freedom of religion and protect religious unity, as such unity was regarded as important to maintain the control of the Crown over the public through the Church. The law only applied to Swedish citizens, while the religious freedom of foreigners was protected by the Tolerance Act.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Conventicle Act restricted religious freedom in Sweden and Finland, leading to a period of limited tolerance for dissenting Christian denominations. The law's impact was most evident during the Great Emigration of Swedes from Russia between 1869-1870.
